title: HIPAA Security Rule Update: Proposal vs Current Duties
summary: HIPAA Security Rule Update: Proposal vs Current Duties: scope, evidence, limitations, and the decisions buyers need to make.
body_markdown:
## What should a health-tech startup do now?


Identify whether and how it acts as a business associate or covered entity, apply the current requirements, and maintain the supporting risk analysis and safeguards. The[HHS Security Rule summary](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/security/laws-regulations/index.html) explains the administrative, physical, and technical safeguard framework.


Use the proposed changes to find operational weaknesses worth addressing now, while documenting which work supports current obligations and which anticipates a possible future rule. A tool purchase or certification label alone does not establish that responsibilities have been met.


## How should customers and vendors discuss the proposal?


State the current requirement, the proposed change, and the source checked. Confirm contractual commitments independently: a customer may request controls in a contract even where a proposal has not become a regulation.


For practical implementation, review[HIPAA support for startups](https://getagency.com/hipaa-for-startups?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=hipaa&utm_content=hipaa-security-rule-proposed-update__in_text) and the[HIPAA service scope](https://getagency.com/frameworks/hipaa?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=hipaa&utm_content=hipaa-security-rule-proposed-update__in_text) . Ask who owns risk analysis, remediation, operating evidence, and incident coordination before signing.
